summary: Backend testing for NOCTUA.osint Pro plan (Stripe + Scheduled Scans + Alerts + Slack). All 23 backend tests passed. Discovered and fixed a critical env load-order bug in server.py causing STRIPE_SECRET_KEY to be missed at import time. Scheduler worker executes within ~65s and correctly stamps scans with source='scheduled' and schedule.last_scan_id.
passed: POST /api/payments/checkout returns checkout_url + session_id, persists payment_transactions with status=initiated/payment_status=pending
POST /api/schedules with pro -> 200; returns schedule_id, domain, frequency, alert_types, enabled=true, next_run_at
GET /api/schedules isolated per user (second user sees empty list)
POST /api/settings/slack valid https://hooks.slack.com/... -> 200 saved and persisted
Scheduler worker: schedule for example.com executed within ~65s (interval=60s), scan stored with source='scheduled' and schedule_id, schedule.last_scan_id populated, next_run_at advanced

minor.issue: Uses hardcoded fallback string 'sk_test_emergent' if STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is missing — would silently 500 with Stripe AuthenticationError. Prefer failing fast (raise) or removing the fallback.
Not signature-verified in this test iteration (per request). Webhook path is /api/stripe/webhook — mounted correctly. No auth wrapper; correct for Stripe callbacks.

critical_code_review_comments: FIXED by testing agent: In server.py, `import payments` and `import schedules` were executed BEFORE `load_dotenv(ROOT_DIR/'.env')`. Because payments.py sets `stripe.api_key = os.environ.get('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY') or 'sk_test_emergent'` at module import time, the real key from backend/.env was never applied and /api/payments/checkout returned 500 (stripe AuthenticationError 'sk_test_****gent'). Moved load_dotenv above the imports. Recommend removing the 'sk_test_emergent' fallback entirely so a missing key fails fast at startup, not at first user checkout.
payments.py imports stripe at module top and configures api_key at import time. Consider lazy configuration or wrapping in a helper so tests/env changes don't require restarts.
schedules.py _diff_ports assumes each port dict has key 'port'; osint_engine returns items like {'port': N, ...}. OK today, but add defensive .get to avoid KeyError on partial results.

schedules.py alert dedup: no idempotency — if scheduler is triggered twice for the same run (e.g., race after restart), duplicate alerts could be created. Consider a unique index on (schedule_id, scan_id, type) or skip if alerts already exist for this scan_id.
server.py .on_event('startup')/('shutdown') are deprecated in FastAPI; migrate to lifespan handler.

payments.py cancel_subscription: after calling stripe.Subscription.delete, code sets plan='free' immediately, but Stripe may take time. Also unsets plan even if the actual subscription id is invalid. Verify via webhook customer.subscription.deleted (already handled). Consider marking pending_cancel and letting the webhook flip plan.
No rate limiting on /api/scan or /api/schedules; a Pro user could create many schedules for expensive domains. Consider max schedules per user.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend Pro-plan surface is green end-to-end. Scheduler is verified live (loop runs every 60s; schedule executes within ~60-90s). Signed Stripe webhook was NOT exercised (unsigned events would be rejected by construct_event). If a webhook drill is needed, either use Stripe CLI to forward with signature, or temporarily bypass STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET verification. If revisiting, run two scheduled executions on iana.org back-to-back and assert alerts collection remains empty.
rca of the issue: SYMPTOM: POST /api/payments/checkout returned 500 with 'Invalid API Key provided: sk_test_****gent'. ROOT CAUSE: server.py imported the `payments` module before calling `load_dotenv`, so at import time payments.py evaluated `stripe.api_key = os.environ.get('STRIPE_SECRET_KEY') or 'sk_test_emergent'` with STRIPE_SECRET_KEY absent, permanently locking Stripe to the fake fallback for the process lifetime. REPRODUCE: (1) leave server.py as-is (imports before load_dotenv); (2) POST /api/payments/checkout with a valid session -> 500. MITIGATION APPLIED: moved `load_dotenv(ROOT_DIR/'.env')` above the `import payments`/`import schedules` lines in server.py. Recommended follow-up: drop the 'sk_test_emergent' fallback so a missing key surfaces immediately at startup rather than at checkout time.
